description: Construction of dormer roof extension to main rear roof, together with installation of three roof lights to front roof and alterations to ground floor rear fenestration to facilitate change of use of 12-person HMO (Use Class Sui Generis) to four self-contained flats (1x3-bed and 3x1-bed) (Class C3) with associated  hard and soft landscaping; refuse and recycling facilities and secure cycle storage.

constraints_details.result: 18 Forest Drive West, Leytonstone, London, E11 1LA

decision_conditions:
The application as submitted relates to the
conversion of a family sized home within a restricted dwelling conversion zone.
Therefore, one of the prerequisites is that the existing gross original
internal floorspace must measure more than 124sq.m. The existing internal floor
space including the ground floor extensions measures 111sq.m, due to this
shortfall the principle of development in relation to Policy 20 (Housing in
Multiple Occupation & Conversions) of the emerging Local Plan could not be
established.

The proposed development contains a
disproportionate level of single occupancy dwellings without justification
contrary to the aims and objectives of Policy 15 of the emerging Local Plan.

The proposed development provides a poor standard
of accommodation for future occupiers in relation to flats 1 & 4,
comprising of (i) combined kitchen, dining and living facilities that fails to
comply with minimum space standards, (ii) floor to ceiling height that fails to
comply with minimum space standards (iii) internal storage area that fails to
comply with minimum space standards, (iv) ineffective use of floor space, and
(v) limited outlook. Therefore, the proposal would be contrary to Policy 56
(Residential Space Standards) of the Emerging Local Plan, Policy D6 of The
London Plan (2021) and London Plan Guidance – Housing Design Standards (June
2023).

In the absence of a Tree Survey (in line with
British Standard 5837:2012 Trees in Relation to Design, Demolition and
Construction), to identify the impact of the development on the existing trees
on site and any other trees located within the vicinity of the development
site, along with the required protection and mitigation measures, a full
assessment of the acceptability of the development and assurance of the
protection of local biodiversity could not be carried out, and therefore it
cannot be confirmed that the development would be in compliance with ﻿Policy 80
of the emerging Local Plan.

The proposed development, fails to make adequate
provision for the storage of combined food & garden waste contrary to
Policy 57 (Amenity) & 93 (Waste Management) of the Emerging Local Plan and
Waste & Recycling Policy for Developers (2022).

The proposed development, fails to make adequate
provision for the external secure storage of 7No. bicycles, contrary to Policy
T5 of the London Plan, Policy 61 and Appendix 1 – Parking standards of the
emerging Local Plan and London Cycle Design Standards (2014).

In the absence of a satisfactory Outline
Construction Logistic Plan, a full assessment of how the proposed
development would be built or serviced without severely affecting the public
highway could not be made in line with Policies T7 of the London Plan (2021)
and Policy 65 of the emerging Local Plan.

The applicant failed to enter into a s106 agreement
and therefore not in compliance with Policy 94 (Infrastructure and Developer
Contributions) of the Emerging Local Pan (figures applicable at the time of the
assessment of the application):Car Free Development - the development is to be
classified as car-free and residents will not be eligible for parking permits.A condition survey of the adjoining
carriageway/footway on Forest Drive West covering a 10 metre dimension,
including a site plan showing the where the photos were taken on the public
highway. Financial contribution of £2,508.00 towards the Epping Forest SAMA S106 contribution of £250 is requested toward CLP
monitoring.A S106 contribution of £3,000 is requested toward
improving walking and cycling facilities within the sites vicinity which will
directly benefit future residents of the site.S278 agreement to remove the 2 dropped kerbs and
reinstate the footway to current standards.Financial contribution of 5% for s106 monitoring
fees.
